lesson.title: Factors, multiples and primes
points: A factor divides a number exactly. A multiple is what you get by multiplying the number by 1, 2, 3 and so on.
A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 2 is the smallest prime and the only even prime. 1 is not prime.
HCF is the highest common factor and LCM is the lowest common multiple of two or more numbers.
A number is divisible by 3 (or 9) when the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 (or 9).
lesson.story: Two buses leave the Hyderabad bus stand together. One goes every 6 minutes and the other every 8 minutes. They leave together again after the LCM of 6 and 8, which is 24 minutes.

example.q: Find the HCF and LCM of 12 and 18.
steps: LCM = every prime at its highest count = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 36.

questions.why: 29 has no factors other than 1 and 29. The others are divisible by 3: 21 = 3 × 7, 27 = 3 × 9 and 39 = 3 × 13.

lesson.title: Numbers below zero
points: Integers are the numbers ... −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 ... They include negative numbers, zero and positive numbers.
On a number line, numbers grow towards the right. So −2 is greater than −5, and every negative number is less than 0.
Adding a positive number moves right. Subtracting a positive number moves left, even past zero.
To compare negative numbers, the one closer to zero is greater.
lesson.story: On a winter night in Leh the temperature is −5°C, while in Chennai it is 28°C. Colder means further left on the number line, so −5 is far smaller than 28.

steps: Start at 3 on the number line.
Move 8 steps to the left: 3 steps reach 0 and 5 more steps go below zero.

lesson.title: Parts of a whole
points: A fraction a/b means a equal parts out of b. Multiplying or dividing the top and bottom by the same number gives an equivalent fraction.
To add or subtract fractions with different denominators, first make the denominators equal using their LCM.
Decimals are fractions with denominators 10, 100, 1000. For example 0.3 = 3/10 and 0.03 = 3/100.
When adding or subtracting decimals, line up the decimal points so the places match.

steps: The LCM of 2 and 3 is 6, so make both denominators 6.

lesson.title: Comparing quantities
points: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, written a : b. Order matters: 3 : 2 is not the same as 2 : 3.
Simplify a ratio by dividing both terms by their common factor, just like a fraction.
Two ratios that are equal form a proportion, for example 2 : 3 = 4 : 6.
To share a total in a ratio, add the parts, find the value of one part, then multiply.

Patterns follow a rule. If a pattern goes 5, 8, 11, 14, it adds 3 each time, and its rule is 3n + 2.
Like terms can be added: 2a + 3a = 5a. The letter stays the same.

lesson.title: Lines, angles and shapes
points: A right angle is 90°, a straight angle is 180° and a full turn is 360°.
Two angles are complementary if they add up to 90° and supplementary if they add up to 180°.
The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°. A triangle is equilateral (3 equal sides), isosceles (2 equal sides) or scalene (no equal sides).
A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves, like a fold line.
lesson.story: Fold a square piece of paper on a rangoli design: along the middle, along the other middle, or along either diagonal. Each fold makes two matching halves, so a square has 4 lines of symmetry.

example.q: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. Find the third angle.
steps: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The two known angles add up to 50° + 60° = 110°.

lesson.title: Around and inside shapes
points: Perimeter is the distance around a shape. For a rectangle it is 2 × (length + breadth) and for a square it is 4 × side.
Area is the space inside a shape, measured in square units like cm² or m². Rectangle area = length × breadth and square area = side × side.
Area of a triangle = 1/2 × base × height.
Use perimeter for fencing or borders and area for tiling or painting.
lesson.story: To put a border of lace around a dupatta, you need its perimeter. To know how many square tiles cover a kitchen floor, you need its area.
